query:
UPDATE services SET
  shortDesc = 'When a municipality''s underground infrastructure starts to fail, every resident on the street feels it. Discount Drain has been the contractor that London and Southwestern Ontario municipalities call when the job has to be done right, on schedule, and with minimal disruption to the public.',
  longDesc = 'Underground municipal infrastructure is unglamorous work, but it is some of the most consequential work we do. A failed sewer main does not just inconvenience one homeowner. It backs up into multiple properties, contaminates groundwater, and can close roads for days. When municipalities in London and Southwestern Ontario face those situations, they need a contractor with the equipment, the crew, and the experience to move fast without cutting corners.\n\nDiscount Drain has been doing this work since 1970. Over five decades, we have handled sewer lining, manhole restoration, water main repair, and large-scale drainage rehabilitation for municipalities, conservation authorities, and commercial property managers across the region. Our fleet includes excavators, combination vac and power flushing trucks, and dump trucks, which means we can mobilize a full crew with the right equipment on short notice rather than waiting on subcontractors.\n\nOne of the most common requests we get from municipal clients is sewer lining. When an aging concrete or clay sewer main has cracked, shifted, or been infiltrated by tree roots, full excavation is not always practical. Our cured-in-place pipe lining process installs a new structural pipe inside the existing one through manhole access points, with no road cutting required. The result is a smooth liner that restores full flow capacity and can extend the service life of the pipe by 50 years or more. For municipalities managing aging infrastructure on constrained budgets, it is often the most cost-effective path forward.\n\nManhole restoration is another area where we see consistent demand. Manholes in Ontario take a beating from freeze-thaw cycles, road salt, heavy vehicle traffic, and decades of use. Deteriorated frames, cracked barrels, and inflow through failing joints are all problems we address regularly. We handle frame and cover replacement, barrel relining, bench and channel repairs, and full manhole reconstruction when the structure has deteriorated beyond repair. Every restoration is inspected with camera equipment before and after to document the condition and confirm the work meets specification.\n\nFor water main repairs and emergency breaks, we respond with our own excavation equipment. We do not rely on third parties to open the ground. When a water main breaks in the middle of a residential street, every hour of downtime affects residents and businesses. Our team can be on site, excavated, and working on the repair faster than most contractors can even mobilize. We also handle service lateral connections, valve replacements, and hydrant repairs as part of our municipal work.',
  benefits = '[{"title":"Rapid Mobilization","description":"Our own fleet of excavators, vac trucks, and dump trucks means we can be on site and working faster than contractors who rely on rented equipment or subcontractors."},{"title":"CIPP Sewer Lining","description":"We install cured-in-place pipe liners that restore structural integrity and flow capacity without excavating roads or disrupting traffic."},{"title":"Full Manhole Restoration","description":"From frame and cover replacement to full barrel reconstruction, we restore manholes to current standards and document every job with pre and post camera inspection."},{"title":"Water Main Repair and Emergency Response","description":"We handle emergency water main breaks with our own excavation crew, minimizing downtime for residents and businesses affected by the outage."},{"title":"Camera Inspection on Every Job","description":"Every municipal drainage job includes a video camera inspection so you have a documented record of the pipe condition before and after our work."},{"title":"55 Years of Infrastructure Experience","description":"Since 1970, we have worked alongside municipalities and conservation authorities across Southwestern Ontario on drainage and sewer infrastructure projects of all scales."}]',
  faqs = '[{"question":"What types of municipal infrastructure does Discount Drain work on?","answer":"We work on sanitary sewer mains, storm sewer systems, manholes, water mains, service laterals, catch basins, and drainage outfalls. We also handle road culvert replacements and large-scale excavation projects for municipalities and conservation authorities."},{"question":"Can you line a sewer main without excavating the road?","answer":"Yes. Our cured-in-place pipe lining process installs a new structural liner inside the existing pipe through access points at manholes. No road cutting is required in most cases. The liner cures in place and restores the pipe to full structural and hydraulic capacity."},{"question":"How long does a CIPP sewer liner last?","answer":"A properly installed CIPP liner has a design life of 50 years or more. The liner is seamless, resistant to root intrusion, and eliminates the joints and cracks that allow groundwater infiltration into the sewer system."},{"question":"What is inflow and infiltration, and why does it matter for municipalities?","answer":"Inflow is stormwater that enters the sanitary sewer system through illegal connections, open manholes, or damaged pipes. Infiltration is groundwater that seeps in through cracks and failed joints. Both increase the volume of flow that wastewater treatment plants must handle, which raises operating costs. Lining and manhole restoration programs reduce inflow and infiltration significantly."},{"question":"Do you handle emergency water main breaks?","answer":"Yes. We offer emergency response for water main breaks with our own excavation equipment. We do not subcontract the excavation, which means we can respond and begin work faster than contractors who need to arrange third-party equipment."},{"question":"Can you work within municipal right-of-way and road allowances?","answer":"Yes. We are fully insured, WSIB compliant, and experienced working within municipal road allowances. We coordinate with the municipality on traffic control, utility locates, and permit requirements before any work begins."},{"question":"What documentation do you provide after a municipal job?","answer":"We provide pre and post camera inspection footage, as-built records for any new installations, and written reports on the condition of the infrastructure before and after our work. Documentation requirements vary by project and we work to meet whatever the municipality specifies."},{"question":"How do you handle traffic control during road-based work?","answer":"We work with certified traffic control personnel and follow the Ontario Traffic Manual requirements for all road-based work. Traffic management plans are prepared in advance and submitted to the municipality or road authority before work begins."},{"question":"Do you work with conservation authorities and provincial agencies?","answer":"Yes. We have experience working with conservation authorities on drainage and culvert projects that fall within regulated areas. We are familiar with the permit requirements and environmental conditions that apply to work near watercourses and wetlands in Ontario."},{"question":"What areas do you serve for municipal work?","answer":"We serve municipalities and public agencies across London and Southwestern Ontario, including the City of London, Middlesex County, Elgin County, Oxford County, and surrounding townships. Contact us to discuss your project and service area."}]',
  imageUrl = 'https://d2xsxph8kpxj0f.cloudfront.net/310519663530669561/Bh4z4tJQ2oLgzVrvga4zYT/municipal-hero-keQHLtRne4Jh7HZy3jDATN.webp',
  metaTitle = 'Municipal Sewer and Drainage Services London Ontario | Discount Drain',
  metaDesc = 'Discount Drain provides municipal sewer lining, manhole restoration, water main repair, and drainage infrastructure services across London and Southwestern Ontario. Family-owned since 1970. Call 519-451-8342.'
WHERE slug = 'municipal-services';
